- **RUL77 (posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". 1. **Account lock.** One lock per provider account under `/account-locks///`, separate from the state lock, in the same append-only generation format. A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The holder records the pid of the renewal child it started: a dead holder with a live child keeps the lock, so a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are capped at five per account, the newest by staging time; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. It also stays held when the pending copies are already full and its login would only be staged, so the cap never pushes out an older copy; a staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the basename of an invocation's `command`: `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's command, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each pane against the store of its own CLI. An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env.

A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. The round's `commit` carries the merge's own record under `sync`; `runUnit` returns `sync` beside `outcome`; a sync-only unit that needed no worker returns one result `{ role: 'sync', round: 0, commit }` (no `verify`, as for `solo`). Not done: an inline producer over an open merge (inline rounds have no runner commit), a modify/delete conflict whose worker deletes the file is concluded as a deletion. - **RUL98 (`fgos workflow start` kế thừa và phân bổ `--timeout ` và `--account ` cho từng Unit, 2026-10-15).** Workflow run hỗ trợ cờ `--timeout ` (chuỗi thời lượng hợp lệ `1m`..`4h`, phân tích ra `timeoutMs`) và `--account ` (ghim tài khoản nhà cung cấp) giống cơ chế của `--effort`. Các lệnh chỉ-đọc như `fgos workflow status` luôn trả về mã thoát 0 bất kể outcome của workflow run. Lệnh `fgos workflow start` ở chế độ detached vẫn trả về mã 0 khi tiến trình daemon được khởi chạy thành công. Định dạng envelope JSON stdout `fgos.v1` giữ nguyên vẹn 100%. - **RUL100 (Doctor check `executor-posture-coverage` chẩn đoán posture readiness của các executor, 2026-10-15).** Check doctor `executor-posture-coverage` kiểm tra tĩnh khả năng áp dụng posture cho các core capabilities (`execute`, `code:implement`) và mọi capability khai báo pool agent (`prefer`). Quá trình kiểm tra chạy hoàn toàn khô qua `bind()`, không spawn tiến trình, không tạo pane herdr, không kích hoạt sandbox. Khi một capability có executor thiếu sandbox bwrap, check báo lỗi `posture-unavailable` (`passed: false`). Khi một capability thiếu pool (`headless-no-executor` / `no-candidate`), check chỉ phát cảnh báo (`passed: true`, tiền tố `warning:`) hướng dẫn khai báo `runner.capabilities..prefer`.

- **RUL101 (the per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock held through holder-lock; a dead holder releases at once, 2026-10-16).** The lock a dispatch takes on its working directory (`dispatch-cwd`, rank 30, kind `lease`, scope still `fgosDir`) is a kernel lock on an open file description, acquired through the holder-lock facade (`src/holder-lock/`, authority `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md`), with the cwd keyed by `dev:ino` after `realpath`. The lock file is `<fgosDir>/locks/dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>.lock`, so one directory reached through a symlink is one lock; a cwd that does not exist fails as `worker-spawn-fail` before any lock. There is no holder record, no `ttlMs`, no heartbeat renewal and no reclaim by a contender: the kernel releases the lock when every process holding the description has died, so a holder killed without releasing, with or without a reused pid, blocks nobody; a live holder that is wedged keeps it until it exits. `sharedCwd` and `forceSharedCwd` still take no lock. A second dispatch on a held cwd fails `dispatch-in-flight` naming the holder pid. The resume guard of `fgos run --resume` and the reconcile planner read the kernel's holder list (`lockHolders`, which takes no lock) and fall back to `probe(dispatch-cwd)` (one non-blocking shared try) only where holders cannot be listed, since a shared try could make a concurrent one-try acquire see `held`; they refuse on a holder, neither judges a holder alive or dead, and a lock that cannot be read is never read as free. The legacy `.fgos/dispatch--<cwd>.lock` path is fenced by a tombstone at cutover for every worktree and claim, in both the `path.resolve` and the `realpath` form; `fgos dispatch reconcile clear-cwd-lock` only reports held or free and never clears a cwd lock. The reconcile planner's own local lock (`reconcile`, rank 80) is a kernel mutex at `<fgosDir>/locks/reconcile.lock` under the same port. Order inside one `LockScope` is enforced at acquire: a lock taken at a rank not above every rank the scope already holds throws `lock-order-violation` at once, with no trace-then-warn release.
- **RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor; llmAccounts is read for checking only, 2026-10-17).** A cell of `runner.modelPolicies.<family>.<tier>` is a model, a model served by a named pool (`model@pool`), or a non-empty ordered list of those. The pool is the service provider that bills the call. A cell entry is split at its last `@`, so a model id that itself contains `@` names its pool explicitly (`claude-opus-4@20250514@vertex`); an entry without `@` is served by the pool named after the family. There is no default-pool key. A run uses the first entry served by the family's own pool (`resolveTierModel`); `resolveTierCandidates` returns every entry for `fgos dispatch explain` and doctor. An entry served by another pool is accepted and never run until the lease routes pools; a cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier, which still falls back to the executor's own `model` or the CLI default. The project config accepts every form. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` is read by every fgOS release on the machine, and an older release fails on a list and passes `model@pool` to the CLI as a model id, so a list or `@` cell there is dropped with a warning naming the cell (once per process), and doctor `global-model-policies-portable` fails on it.
  Each agent family (`providerModel`) is served by exactly one executor; its transports (headless cli, herdr pane, sandboxed or not) are invocations of that executor, and `bind()` picks the pane invocation inside herdr and a cli one outside, so a capability gets the same family and model in both places. Doctor `executor-family-unique` fails on a family with two agent executors.
  `runner.llmAccounts.<pool>.<account>` is the machine's account inventory, global-only: `credentialStore: { <cli>: <login directory> }` (`~`, `${HOME}` and `$HOME` expand), plus optional `label` and `disabled`. A pool name is the family name for the family's own vendor and the provider's name otherwise (`openrouter`); it may not contain `@` nor be another spelling of a configured family (`codex`, `openai-codex`, `glm`, `agy`). `readLlmAccounts` reports problems instead of throwing; `compareWithLegacyInventory` sets it against `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts` by the state key the lease uses (`openai` is `openai-codex` there). The lease, account pins and credential provisioning still read `runner.providers` only. Doctor: `llm-accounts-shape` fails on any reader problem, `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` warns on accounts or login directories that differ once `llmAccounts` is declared, `model-policy-pools` warns on a cell naming a pool `llmAccounts` does not declare.
  `fgos dispatch explain --for <capability> [--rigor <r>]` binds the capability through `bind()` and reports the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier, its source (rigor, override) and its ceiling (RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling)), the whole cell with each entry marked `used`, `fallback-same-pool` or `pending-pool-routing`, the executor and invocation, and the pool's accounts in both inventories. It leases, spawns and writes nothing.
- **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(<capability>, <rigor>)`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(<tier>, <ceiling source>)`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose.

1. **Account lock.** One lock per provider account under `<runtime dir>/account-locks/<provider>/<account>/`, separate from the state lock, in the same append-only generation format. A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The holder records the pid of the renewal child it started: a dead holder with a live child keeps the lock, so a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token.

4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are capped at five per account, the newest by staging time; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. It also stays held when the pending copies are already full and its login would only be staged, so the cap never pushes out an older copy; a staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal.

unit.text:

The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". 1. **Account lock.** One lock per provider account under `/account-locks///`, separate from the state lock, in the same append-only generation format. A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The holder records the pid of the renewal child it started: a dead holder with a live child keeps the lock, so a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. - **RUL101 (the per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock held through holder-lock; a dead holder releases at once, 2026-10-16).** The lock a dispatch takes on its working directory (`dispatch-cwd`, rank 30, kind `lease`, scope still `fgosDir`) is a kernel lock on an open file description, acquired through the holder-lock facade (`src/holder-lock/`, authority `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md`), with the cwd keyed by `dev:ino` after `realpath`. The lock file is `<fgosDir>/locks/dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>.lock`, so one directory reached through a symlink is one lock; a cwd that does not exist fails as `worker-spawn-fail` before any lock. There is no holder record, no `ttlMs`, no heartbeat renewal and no reclaim by a contender: the kernel releases the lock when every process holding the description has died, so a holder killed without releasing, with or without a reused pid, blocks nobody; a live holder that is wedged keeps it until it exits. `sharedCwd` and `forceSharedCwd` still take no lock. A second dispatch on a held cwd fails `dispatch-in-flight` naming the holder pid. The resume guard of `fgos run --resume` and the reconcile planner read the kernel's holder list (`lockHolders`, which takes no lock) and fall back to `probe(dispatch-cwd)` (one non-blocking shared try) only where holders cannot be listed, since a shared try could make a concurrent one-try acquire see `held`; they refuse on a holder, neither judges a holder alive or dead, and a lock that cannot be read is never read as free. The legacy `.fgos/dispatch--<cwd>.lock` path is fenced by a tombstone at cutover for every worktree and claim, in both the `path.resolve` and the `realpath` form; `fgos dispatch reconcile clear-cwd-lock` only reports held or free and never clears a cwd lock. The reconcile planner's own local lock (`reconcile`, rank 80) is a kernel mutex at `<fgosDir>/locks/reconcile.lock` under the same port. Order inside one `LockScope` is enforced at acquire: a lock taken at a rank not above every rank the scope already holds throws `lock-order-violation` at once, with no trace-then-warn release.
- **RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool; one family has one executor; llmAccounts is read for checking only, 2026-10-17).** A cell of `runner.modelPolicies.<family>.<tier>` is a model, a model served by a named pool (`model@pool`), or a non-empty ordered list of those. The pool is the service provider that bills the call. A cell entry is split at its last `@`, so a model id that itself contains `@` names its pool explicitly (`claude-opus-4@20250514@vertex`); an entry without `@` is served by the pool named after the family. There is no default-pool key. A run uses the first entry served by the family's own pool (`resolveTierModel`); `resolveTierCandidates` returns every entry for `fgos dispatch explain` and doctor. An entry served by another pool is accepted and never run until the lease routes pools; a cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier, which still falls back to the executor's own `model` or the CLI default. The project config accepts every form. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` is read by every fgOS release on the machine, and an older release fails on a list and passes `model@pool` to the CLI as a model id, so a list or `@` cell there is dropped with a warning naming the cell (once per process), and doctor `global-model-policies-portable` fails on it.
  Each agent family (`providerModel`) is served by exactly one executor; its transports (headless cli, herdr pane, sandboxed or not) are invocations of that executor, and `bind()` picks the pane invocation inside herdr and a cli one outside, so a capability gets the same family and model in both places. Doctor `executor-family-unique` fails on a family with two agent executors.
  `runner.llmAccounts.<pool>.<account>` is the machine's account inventory, global-only: `credentialStore: { <cli>: <login directory> }` (`~`, `${HOME}` and `$HOME` expand), plus optional `label` and `disabled`. A pool name is the family name for the family's own vendor and the provider's name otherwise (`openrouter`); it may not contain `@` nor be another spelling of a configured family (`codex`, `openai-codex`, `glm`, `agy`). `readLlmAccounts` reports problems instead of throwing; `compareWithLegacyInventory` sets it against `runner.providers.<provider>.accounts` by the state key the lease uses (`openai` is `openai-codex` there). The lease, account pins and credential provisioning still read `runner.providers` only. Doctor: `llm-accounts-shape` fails on any reader problem, `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` warns on accounts or login directories that differ once `llmAccounts` is declared, `model-policy-pools` warns on a cell naming a pool `llmAccounts` does not declare.
  `fgos dispatch explain --for <capability> [--rigor <r>]` binds the capability through `bind()` and reports the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier, its source (rigor, override) and its ceiling (RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling)), the whole cell with each entry marked `used`, `fallback-same-pool` or `pending-pool-routing`, the executor and invocation, and the pool's accounts in both inventories. It leases, spawns and writes nothing.
- **RUL103 (runner.maxTier caps every seat; a capability's own rigor raises its own ceiling, 2026-10-17).** `runner.maxTier`, when set, is the highest tier a seat runs at, whatever asked for the tier: the unit's rigor, the capability's rigor floor, or an override (`--override '{"tier":...}'`). A capability that declares its own `rigor` in `runner.capabilities` raises the ceiling for its own seats to `rigorToTier[rigor]` when that tier is higher. The ceiling of a seat is therefore the higher of `runner.maxTier` and the tier of its capability's declared rigor (`resolveTierCeiling` in `bind.mjs`); a unit's rigor and an override stay under it, so only the config decides which capabilities may run above the cap, and a frontier override on a capability declaring `high` stops at `flagship`. Without `runner.maxTier` there is no ceiling. A capability cannot be held below the global cap this way. The binding records the ceiling on `provenance.tier.ceiling` as `{ value, source }`, `source` being `global` or `capability-rigor(<capability>, <rigor>)`; a clamped tier's source reads `clamped:maxTier(<tier>, <ceiling source>)`. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the ceiling, and doctor `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted above `runner.maxTier` with the tier and model they run at; it never fails. The assignment policy (`resolveAssignmentDispatchPolicy`) raises the tier `bind()` hands it and applies no ceiling, so when `bind()` clamped, the policy's recorded tier can read higher than the tier that ran; the model is always the one `bind()` chose.

changedSourceLines.text: - **RUL77 (posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute <id> --for <capability>` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor.<id>.agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities.<name>.prefer`). The CLI door `execute <agent>` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute <agent> --for <capability>` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract <file> --executor <id>` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any".

1. **Account lock.** One lock per provider account under `<runtime dir>/account-locks/<provider>/<account>/`, separate from the state lock, in the same append-only generation format. A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The holder records the pid of the renewal child it started: a dead holder with a live child keeps the lock, so a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token.

4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per account, but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal.

- **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`.

- **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ <cli>: <source> }`, the key is the basename of an invocation's `command`: `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/stores/<cli>/` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each pane against the store of its own CLI. An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env.

The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the basename of an invocation's `command`: `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's command, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each pane against the store of its own CLI. An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. Not built: per-CLI stores for an unconfined invocation, which keeps naming its store through its own env.

selected.sample: **Architecture advisory — current boundary.** `core/skills/fgos-architecture-panel/SKILL.md` starts registered Workflows, reads settled reports, and exposes public `workflow status
selected.text:
**Architecture advisory — current boundary.** `core/skills/fgos-architecture-panel/SKILL.md` starts registered Workflows, reads settled reports, and exposes public `workflow status`/`workflow answer` commands for the owner's declared gate; it owns no raw run-state driver or executor roster. `architecture-advisory` has five linear execution steps plus human close, with distinct panel-seat lenses and reviewed/high final synthesis; `architecture-advisory-reopen` revisits parent reports through synthesis → explanation → close without blind seats. Both synthesis templates require reviewer and red-team regardless of configured high-rigor checker defaults. Executor/provider/model/invocation selection remains config + `bind()` owned. Required read-only posture refuses unsafe execution.
`council-lite` is a one-panel discussion Workflow: `params.roleTasks` gives each seat one task posture from `core/agents/council-*.yaml`, supplied through template `contextRefs`. Each description contains method, blind spot, and an explicit evidence-led ending rule; posture is not actor identity, registry membership, or provider policy. `bind()` spreads seats across provider families as a preference (decision 0055), never refusing a seat for sharing one. No runtime or renderer seam is added. Each seat first writes a short "Restatement" of the question and what it treats as out of scope before analysing, and the synthesizer lists mismatched restatements as unresolved evidence.
`workflow start --seats "<lens>|<lens>|..."` rebuilds a registered base whose panels are generic (`group-cognition`, `business-discussion`, `nominal-group`, `delphi`) with one panel seat per lens (decision 0056). A panel unit is generic when its `params.roleTasks` has no `panelist-N` key and it sets no custom `params.role`; a base with no generic panel, or with any curated one (`council-lite`, `architecture-advisory`), is refused with the reason, so lenses never overwrite curated seats. The Workflow component (`src/workflow/seats.mjs`, called from `prepareWorkflowRun`) clones the loaded base and, on every generic panel unit, sets `params.members = N` and `roleTasks.panelist-1..N` from one runtime-owned sentence that frames the lens as a task focus and ends in `{objective}`; Delphi gets the same seats in both rounds so `sameSeat` inputs stay aligned. Steps, `dependsOn`, gates, `blind`, checker and synthesizer text are untouched and the result is revalidated by the same validator. Entries: at least 2, no schema maximum, distinct case-insensitively; a lens is 3-160 characters on one line without braces or `|`; an entry `@name` (`[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}` after the `@`) seats a named persona on that panel seat alone (decision 0057). Run-level `--context-ref` reaches only root steps, so with `--seats` the shared refs are also copied into the template of every unit in a step that depends on another. Before the run is recorded the CLI dry-binds the expanded panel units (`preflightWorkflowSeats`, `simulateUnitBindings`): seats that would share a provider family are returned as `seatsPreflight.warnings` (informational), and a role no candidate can serve refuses the start; nothing is created in either case. The expanded definition is stored in the existing `workflow.start` event with a provenance record `seats: { seats, baseId, baseDigest, refs }` and the status projection exposes `seats`; resume and status read stored data and never re-expand, and `workflow resume --seats` refuses seats that differ from the stored ones. Without `--seats` the definition, event and projection are unchanged.
A named persona is looked up once by `src/runner/agent-definitions.mjs`: workspace `fgos/agents/<name>.yaml` of the working project, then `domains/*/agents/`, then `core/agents/` (a project without its own `domains/` or `core/agents/` folder reads the installed package's), whole-file replacement across tiers, two files of one name in one tier is an error, an unknown name is an error that lists every folder searched, and a file must declare `name:` equal to its basename and a non-empty `description:`. `prepareWorkflowRun` resolves every name before the run exists and records `seats.personas: [{ seat, name, tier, source, digest, text }]` (the exact file bytes and their SHA-256) in the same `workflow.start` event; the status projection exposes it. The runner emits, for every panel unit, one override `{ scope: { unit, role: "panelist-N" }, persona, personaPin, origin: "workflow" }` per named seat ahead of the unit-wide persona override, so `bind()` (first matching override, unchanged) gives the persona to that seat only; the synthesizer and checkers never inherit it. `run.mjs` copies the pin of the matching override onto the assignment's `policy.personaPin`, and `renderPersonaSection` renders the pinned text through the same parser instead of reading a file, so resume and later steps never re-read the live file. A lens seat keeps the runtime lens sentence; a named seat has no lens task and keeps the unit's objective as its task.
Reviewed templates alone may declare `acceptOutcomes: [pass, findings]`; omission remains pass-only. Evidenced `done`/`findings` retains completed execution and findings on both read-only and mutating settlement branches; this does not imply approval or permission to advance mutating work. Coding feature validation and implementation retain revision followed by step failure if findings remain. Business discussion, group cognition, advisory critique/synthesis and marketing draft-copy opt in explicitly; marketing still parks for human approval. Findings never excuse transport/execution failure.
The coding driver honors an explicit operation-choice repair route or canProceed before the generic satisfied gate; explicit stop still wins. Thus review REJECT/findings routes to fix-verify-red, while plan NOT READY/findings stays on the planning path. Mutating producer findings leaves dirty work uncommitted. Claude herdr grants only the current run, copied inputs and canonical parent directories of existing absolute file contextRefs; this is prompt-policy preparation, not expanded OS confinement or live proof.
Repeatable `workflow start --context-ref <ref>` uses the template validator and persists one `contextRefs` field in the start event/projection, delivered to every Unit in a root step; template refs remain local to their owning Unit. Cross-repo launches reject plain paths before run creation: use state-root `unit-run:<id>/<role>` or `gate-answer:<run>/<step>` refs. Linked worktrees of the same repository retain plain-path support. No extra capture/provenance state is introduced.
The final producer report must be a RAW JSON object with `"missing expertise": []` or nonblank string entries. The new `{{report:synthesis/synthesize-recommendation:missing expertise}}` reference in a human `gate.question` reads the settled, hash-verified producer report and renders the fixed batched close. The field is read under either spelling (`missing expertise` or `missing_expertise`); when the report itself is prose, a `packet-*.json` object beside it counts only if it was not modified after the report settled, because the report digest does not cover it. Fenced or prose-embedded JSON is never parsed. Malformed or absent reports park with a clear error and no inferred expertise; resume remains parked, and the owner may answer after manual review with an acknowledged limitation.

next.text: **`fgos workflow start` không giữ người gọi.** Một run kéo dài từ vài phút tới hàng chục phút, nên `start` chỉ ghi run vào event log (`.fgos/workflow-runs/<id>/events.jsonl`) rồi trả ngay `workflowRunId` cùng `detached: { pid, logPath, statusCommand }`; việc chạy tiếp do một process tách rời (`fgos workflow resume <id>`, stdout/stderr vào `advance.log` cạnh event log) đảm nhận — sống sót khi người gọi thoát hoặc bị `timeout` kill, và không mồ côi pane herdr. Tiến độ đọc qua `fgos workflow status <id>` (cùng event log, không kênh phụ); câu hỏi treo vẫn trả lời qua `fgos workflow answer`. `answer` và `resume` cũng vậy: `answer` ghi câu trả lời đồng bộ (step/answer sai vẫn lỗi ngay) rồi giao việc chạy tiếp cho process tách rời và trả cùng khối `detached`; `resume` chỉ giao việc chạy tiếp. Một mẫu duy nhất: process tách rời chính là `fgos workflow resume <id> --foreground`, nên không đệ quy. `--foreground` giữ run trong chính process gọi tới khi completed/failed/parked (dùng cho test và người cần chặn tới kết quả). Cùng mẫu với `fgos gateway start` (spawn `detached`, `unref`, log ra file). Một run chỉ có một process chạy tiếp tại một thời điểm: process đang chạy giữ kernel mutex `.fgos/workflow-runs/<id>/locks/advance.lock` (holder-lock), advance thứ hai bị từ chối với thông báo rõ nêu pid holder và không ghi gì (kể cả câu trả lời); process giữ lock chết thì kernel nhả ngay. `advance.running`/pid đọc từ danh sách holder của kernel, không lấy lock nào. Run đang chạy nền cũng quan sát được mà không phải đọc `events.jsonl`: process tách rời ghi vào `advance.log` một dòng khi mỗi step bắt đầu, kết thúc, thất bại hoặc đỗ chờ trả lời (suy ra từ chính các event đã ghi, không kho trạng thái thứ hai; run chạy `--foreground` không tự in dòng nào), và `fgos workflow status <id>` thêm khối `advance: { running, pid, logPath, lastLines, hint }` — `running`/`pid` lấy từ cùng phép kiểm sống của `advance.lock`, `lastLines` là đuôi (20 dòng cuối, mỗi dòng tối đa 300 ký tự) của `advance.log` khi run chưa `completed` và log không rỗng; khi run còn `running` mà không process nào giữ lock và event cuối đã cũ (hơn 30 giây), `hint` nói advance không chạy và nêu `fgos workflow resume <id>` để chạy tiếp (trường hợp process con chết trước khi kịp ghi event).

sourceWitness.text: **Vai mù thật sự (`blind`) — chặn đọc run state của peer.** Mặc định tắt (không đổi hành vi). Một cờ ở Unit (và ở `template` của Workflow): `blind: true` làm *mọi vai* của Unit chạy với `hostRead: blind` (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` §9.2): worker không đọc được `.fgos/assignments`, `.fgos/workflow-runs`, `.fgos/dispatch-runs` của project, thư mục socket herdr, private home của dispatch khác, hay `/proc/<pid>` của tiến trình anh em; chỉ đọc được thư mục của chính nó (brief, ref đã được trao — chỉ-đọc) và ghi outbox. Phần còn lại của host (repo, `node`, DNS) và file tracked trong `.fgos` không đổi. Unit `blind` không bao giờ chạy không-blind: nếu không thực thi được — `bind()` không chọn in-process/inline, không có bwrap, mode không `required`, probe hỏng/chưa tươi, `cwd` hay ref nằm trong vùng bị che — dispatch bị từ chối trước khi spawn với lý do có tên (`blind-in-process`, `blind-requires-confinement`, `blind-hides-workspace`, `blind-ref-hidden`, `confinement-probe-failed`, ...). Với Unit `blind`, input `unit-run:`/`gate-answer:` (và ref bất kỳ nằm trong vùng bị che) không được giao bằng đường dẫn gốc: lúc dispatch, `resolveUnitInputs` + `copyHandoffsInto` chép nguyên byte (kiểm sha256) vào `inputs/` của round dir của chính vai đó, mỗi vai một bản, tên trung tính khi có `anonymizeInputs`; `unit.json` giữ `inputMap`, resume dùng lại bản chép. `blind-ref-hidden` chỉ còn cho ref không chép được. Workflow bật `blind`: hai bước panel của `delphi` (`propose-round-1`, `propose-round-2`), `generate-ideas` của `nominal-group`, `sense-making-panel` của `group-cognition`; `architecture-advisory` và `business-discussion` chưa bật vì pool của chúng gồm agy, họ chưa qua canary blind.

previous.text: **Ẩn danh đầu vào (`anonymizeInputs`) — vai mù thật sự cần che "ai nói".** Mặc định tắt (không đổi hành vi). Một cờ duy nhất, `anonymizeInputs: true`, ở Unit (và ở `template` của Workflow, đi thẳng vào Unit): khi bật, mỗi `unit-run:` trong `inputs` không còn được trao bằng đường dẫn gốc (có tên seat và unit run id) mà được chép nguyên byte (sau khi qua kiểm sha256 như thường) vào `<unitDir>/inputs/seat-A.md`, `seat-B.md`, ... theo thứ tự danh sách `inputs` (người gọi quyết định thứ tự; không xáo trộn, không cấu hình thêm), và chỉ các bản chép đó vào `contextRefs`, sau các ref khác. Bảng tên trung tính → input gốc nằm trong `unit.json` (`inputMap`), không bao giờ vào brief; resume dùng lại đúng danh sách và bản chép. Runner Workflow, khi bật, viết objective chỉ với `### seat-A` + dòng `Summary` của vai đó — không còn tên bước, unit, unit run hay vai. Đường dẫn repo và câu trả lời cổng của owner (`gate-answer:`) giữ nguyên, vì đó là của owner chứ không ẩn danh. Lỗi nêu rõ và xảy ra trước dispatch: run/vai/report thiếu, `report-changed-after-settle`, hoặc `copy-failed`. Giới hạn nói thẳng: đây chỉ là *ẩn danh theo cách dựng thứ được trao*, KHÔNG ngăn một worker chủ động đi tìm — worker vẫn đọc được các file khác trong `.fgos/assignments/` (kể cả outbox của panelist anh em) cho tới khi có giới hạn đọc ở lớp confinement; và nội dung report tự nó có thể lộ giọng/tự xưng. Không áp cho truyền trong-run của pattern (synthesizer của `panel` vẫn nhận report theo tên panelist, vì nó được dặn nêu vị trí từng panelist): muốn tổng hợp mù thì tách thành bước Workflow riêng với `anonymizeInputs`. `core/workflows/delphi.yaml` bật cờ này ở bước tổng hợp phản hồi và vòng hai (Delphi vốn đòi ẩn danh); các Workflow khác để nguyên. Ví dụ bước đối chất: `{ id: cross-examine, dependsOn: [opinions], units: [{ id: x, template: { capability: ..., pattern: solo, objective: "Chỉ ra chỗ yếu của từng ý kiến", anonymizeInputs: true } }] }`.

next.text: **Chọn kết quả nào của bước trước đi vào bước này (`inputs` ở `template` của Workflow).** Mặc định không đổi: một unit nhận report của mọi vai ở mọi bước mà bước của nó phụ thuộc (trực tiếp hay gián tiếp). Khi `template` khai `inputs`, unit chỉ nhận đúng các bước được liệt kê, theo thứ tự liệt kê: `{ step: <id>, sameSeat?: true, label?: <chữ> }`. `{ step }` là report của mọi vai ở mọi unit của bước đó (như mặc định, kể cả việc đặt tên `seat-A`... khi có `anonymizeInputs`). `sameSeat: true` là kết quả của *chính ghế của vai nhận* ở bước đó: panelist `panelist-2` của bước này nhận report của `panelist-2` ở bước trước, không nhận của ghế khác. `label` là chữ do tác giả viết, hiện cạnh mục đó trong brief (ví dụ `group summary`); không có thì brief giữ cách ghi cũ. Câu trả lời cổng của owner (`gate-answer:`) không thuộc `inputs` và vẫn đi theo mặc định. Loader từ chối trước khi chạy: `inputs` không phải mảng, mục không phải object hay có khóa lạ, thiếu `step`, `step` không khai báo hoặc không phải bước mà bước này phụ thuộc (trực tiếp hay gián tiếp). Về cơ chế vẫn chỉ một bộ phân giải (`handoff-refs.mjs`): runner Workflow đưa vào `inputs` của Unit ref `unit-run:<unitRunId>/{seat}`; `{seat}` là chỗ giữ duy nhất, không thuộc unit nào nên `resolveUnitInputs` bỏ qua nó khi tạo unit run, và khi dispatch từng vai, `run.mjs` gọi lại `resolveUnitInputs` với `seat` = tên vai để ra đúng report của vai đó (cùng kiểm sha256), rồi `copyHandoffsInto` chép vào `inputs/own-previous.<đuôi>` trong thư mục của chính vai (cả khi unit `blind` lẫn không). Ghế mà run trước không có (ví dụ bước trước chạy `solo`, bước này chạy `panel`) bị từ chối tại lúc vai đó dispatch với lý do `no-such-seat`; panel nào cũng chạy thêm vai `synthesizer`, nên vai này của bước này nhận kết quả `synthesizer` của bước trước. Brief chỉ nói "file `own-previous` là thứ chính bạn đã làm ở bước trước", không nêu tên ghế khác. Ví dụ Delphi vòng hai (`core/workflows/delphi.yaml`, `propose-round-2`): `inputs: [{ step: feedback-synthesis, label: group summary }, { step: blind-proposals, sameSeat: true, label: your own previous proposal }]` cho mỗi panelist bản tổng hợp ẩn danh (`seat-A`) cộng đề xuất vòng một của chính nó, không còn đề xuất thô của các panelist khác.

sourceWitness.text:
- **Trạng thái:** Settled (Request-to-Run P1 Execution Core hoàn tất, 2026-10-01)
- **Bối cảnh:** L5 trước P1 bị phân mảnh: "ai làm" bị quyết định ở nhiều nơi (coordination engine, `decide`, placement-policy, `assignment-policy.mjs`); "chạy qua cửa nào" có nhiều cửa ad-hoc; read-only bị chia rẽ giữa invocation `*-readonly` và tool gating; cổng ghi file phụ thuộc template stamp của engine.
- **Quyết định:**
  1. **Hợp đồng Unit (`src/runner/execution/unit.mjs`):** Hợp đồng dữ liệu duy nhất cho mọi đường vào. Phi hạ tầng (G2) — cấm chứa executor/provider/model/tier/invocation/actors/prefer/overrides.
  2. **Một `bind()` duy nhất (`src/runner/execution/bind.mjs`):** Bảng 5 mức (Session -> Overrides -> Unit role/rigor -> Project taste -> Global taste), tái dùng `mechanism.mjs` theo D-ADR0033 (một cơ chế dispatch).
  3. **Một cửa chạy `fgos run` (`src/runner/execution/run.mjs`):** Bọc `executeAssignment`, mặc định spawn qua pane herdr (G7), cli fallback. Có `fgos run record` cho producer inline với nonce một lần phát kèm chỉ dẫn và kiểm chứng `evidenceRefs`.
  4. **3 Pattern cộng tác (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`):** Vòng lặp code nhỏ, thuần, không store mới (Q-B: trạng thái vòng lặp suy từ `history()` của Unit run). `findings` là outcome, không đánh `failed`.
  5. **Cổng ghi file kiểm chứng được (supersede ADR-006 §6):** Assignment `mutating` được admit khi: (a) cwd là linked worktree và `realpath(cwd) == unit.json.worktree`, (b) `bind()` tính lại từ `unit.json` khớp deep-equal. Ngoại lệ có tên: engine protocol stamp giữ tới P4 phase 6. D-ADR0033 (một cơ chế dispatch) giữ nguyên.
  6. **Xoá bỏ hoàn toàn:** Invocations `*-readonly`, `readOnlyRedirects`, `placement-policy.mjs`, `executors.*.for`, PolicyPatch `prefer*`. Posture read-only/ghi file là confinement OS do fgOS áp cho cả herdr lẫn cli (X-1). Quota limit `provider-limit` kích hoạt `bind().nextCandidate` mở pane mới giữ pane cũ (X-3).
Đổi quyết định này = supersede bằng record mới, không sửa tại chỗ.
